title: Invocation harness: parallel-safe ergonomics and OpenAI compatibility adaptor
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a safer invocation harness for parallel tool execution with deterministic result injection and an OpenAI-compatible adaptor for function calling. Opt-in via feature flag; no immediate public breaking changes.
description:
Summary: This PR introduces a new invocation harness that standardizes multi-tool and parallel tool execution ergonomics, ensures deterministic tool-result injection across retries, and includes an OpenAI-compatible adaptor for function calls and structured output maps. The goal is to make tool orchestration easier for SDK users while improving streaming stability and retry safety.

Motivation: We have recurring issues where parallel tool calls race on result injection into the streamed response, causing inconsistent structured output and broken function-calling behavior for OpenAI-compatible clients. Additionally, retries were sometimes re-injecting partial results or duplicating side-effects when tool invocations were not idempotent. This change centralizes invocation lifecycle management to address these problems and provide a migration path for clients.

What changed (high level):
- New invocation harness that serializes final injection points while allowing parallel execution of tool calls. This minimizes tail latency while guaranteeing deterministic result ordering when injecting JSON/structured outputs.
- Retry-safe execution: harness tracks per-invocation idempotency tokens and replay guards so retries do not double-inject results or re-run non-idempotent actions without explicit allowlist.
- OpenAI compatibility adaptor: a translator layer that maps Redwood tool-calling primitives to OpenAI-style function_call responses, including name/arguments shaping and structured output enforcement. The adaptor is opt-in via redwood.experimental.openai_adaptor flag.
- Streaming improvements: handshake changes to streaming protocol to allow late-bound injection of JSON blocks with backpressure-resistant framing to prevent partial JSON emission during cancellations.
- SDK ergonomics: small TS and Python SDK helpers added to make it straightforward for clients to register tools with signatures that the adaptor consumes.

Files changed (high level):
- redwood/api/invocation/harness.go: main harness implementation and idempotency guard (new).
- redwood/api/invocation/streaming_protocol.proto: handshake updates and new injection frame type.
- redwood/openai_compat/adaptor.go: mapping layer and tests (new).
- sdk/typescript/src/tools.ts: helper utilities for registering tools with signature metadata.
- sdk/python/redwood/tools.py: Python SDK helpers and docstrings.
- infra/feature_flags.yaml: experimental flag for the adaptor.
- tests/integration/invocation_parallel_test.go: deterministic parallel invocation tests.
- tests/openai_compat/function_call_flow.test.ts: end-to-end adaptor tests.
- docs/api/tool_invocation.md: user-facing migration and examples.

Commits (summary):
- 8a4b930: add invocation harness with idempotency token tracking
- b1d0c42: implement streaming injection frame and handshake
- d5e8f11: create openai compatibility adaptor and mapping logic
- f3c2aa8: SDK helpers (TS/Python) and docs
- 9b7a2fe: add integration tests and flakiness mitigations
- 2c4f901: small perf tweak for parallel scheduling and unit test fixes

Testing:
- Added deterministic unit/integration tests that simulate interleaved tool completions and ensure a single deterministic injection point into the streamed response.
- End-to-end tests validate OpenAI-style function_call responses for both single-tool and multi-tool compositions.
- Load tests show no regression in 95th percentile latency with parallel execution enabled; small improvement in tail latency for workloads with high KV cache reuse due to better scheduling.

Backward compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior unchanged; new harness is gateable behind redwood.experimental.invocation_harness and the OpenAI adaptor behind redwood.experimental.openai_adaptor. We plan a staged rollout: start with internal canary, opt-in beta customers, then wider rollout after two weeks of telemetry.
- SDK helpers are additive; existing registration APIs remain supported.

Checklist (author):
- [x] New harness code with unit tests
- [x] Integration and end-to-end tests for OpenAI adaptor
- [x] Documentation with migration examples and feature flag instructions
- [x] Performance smoke test
- [x] Feature flag wired into infra

Review conversation (condensed):
- Miguel Santos: "Nice isolation of idempotency logic. Can we make the token boundary pluggable so Dedicated customers with KMS policies can control token generation?"
- Aisha Patel: "Yes, added a token provider interface and default implementation that uses the runtime KMS. Documented how to supply a custom provider in the private installer."

- Claire Nguyen: "The streaming framing change looks solid, but I'm worried about SDK ergonomics for incremental builders. Can you add an example that shows partial tool output aggregation before final injection?"
- Aisha Patel: "Added TS/Python examples in docs and a test that mimics incremental aggregation and final injection."

- Omar Rahman: "Tests look good; two suggestions: (1) add a regression test for the incident ENG-3625 where duplicate tool execution appeared; (2) move the default for the adaptor flag to 'off' and make rollout explicit in infra."
- Aisha Patel: "Added the regression test and left the adaptor flag off by default as requested."

CI and gating:
- CI: unit tests, linters, and integration suite passed on the final run. Some flaky tests were stabilized (retry backoff adjustments).
- Canary: deployed to internal canary cluster behind feature flag; observed stable streaming and no increased error budget during 48h.

Merge outcome:
- Merged via squash by release-bot after approvals from Miguel and Claire and green CI. Merge commit: 'squash-92755-1f2e7d'.

Notes and follow-ups:
- Follow-up ticket ENG-4369 created to add telemetry hooks for injection latency and retry events.
- Consider adding an allowlist manifest for non-idempotent tools that require explicit compensation actions; tracked in ENG-4392.

If you want to test locally: see docs/api/tool_invocation.md for examples of registering a sample tool with a schema and driving the OpenAI adaptor flow.
